clue.text: Somewhat evident if you recognise what a thing is

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather obvious remark about working out what something is.
explanation.definitionFit: To pin down or name what an object is, is to put a name to it: the phrase is a straight paraphrase.

clue.text: Press is and isn't organised

indicators.note: organised signals the letters of is and isn't are arranged into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving its four letters

explanation.surface: A paradox about the press both existing and being disorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is a verb: urge.
explanation.definitionFit: To press a point is to urge or demand firmly, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Quits accepting last of test results

indicators.note: accepting says the word for quits takes in the picked letter

parts.note: being quits means being even or square, hence evens

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word test

explanation.surface: Someone quitting after accepting test results.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcomes are results, and also events: things that come about as consequences.

clue.text: Blunders and removes clothes, going topless

indicators.note: going topless says the first letter is dropped, the top of a down entry

parts.note: to undress is to strip

explanation.surface: Someone making slips while undressing and baring their chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumbles or slips, literal or figurative, are mistakes: synonyms for blunders.

clue.text: Little folks' charity bazaar is gathering energy

definitions.note: a possessive plural; the answer stands for the little folk themselves

parts.note: a fair is a bazaar raising funds for charity

indicators.note: gathering says is collects the letter for energy within it

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Children's charity fair is picking up momentum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little folks' is a traditional name for elves and fairies, not children.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'little folk' or 'little people' of folklore are sprites and elves.

clue.text: Singular units of linear measure for beams

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
miles are units for measuring length or distance

explanation.surface: A dry entry from a measurement textbook, describing units of length for beams of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like timber being measured, but it is the verb: someone beams, i.e. grins broadly.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to grin broadly, so beams is a synonym for grins in the third person.

clue.text: Rodent pinching upset hospital cat's facial hair

indicators.note: pinching says the rodent grabs the jumbled letters and holds them inside

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

indicators.note: upset says the letters of cat are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A mouse stealing a sick cat's whiskers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CAT into TAC; with H after it, 'pinching' puts the lot inside the rodent. 'hospital cat' reads as one animal but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is a type of facial hair; an example of the category.

clue.text: Auditor of catalogue before intermittently lean years

indicators.note: before says the catalogue word comes first

parts.note: a catalogue is a list

indicators.note: intermittently picks alternate letters from lean years, starting with the second

explanation.surface: An auditor's catalogue covering some years of financial hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, but here it is literally one who hears.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor in its root sense is one who hears, from Latin audire, so a hearer.

clue.text: Uncertainty of opinion about US policies primarily

indicators.note: about says the opinion word wraps around US and the picked letter

parts.note: sense can mean opinion, as in 'the sense of the meeting'

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of policies

explanation.surface: Doubt in public opinion about American policies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense uncertainty about how things will turn out is suspense; a near-synonym.

clue.text: Precise brief conjecture whenever in charge

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a conjecture
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: Someone praising a short guess that is accurate whenever an expert is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exact and particular is said to be precise; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Surmise about tense invitees

indicators.note: about says the word for surmise goes around the letter for tense

parts.note: to surmise is to guess
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A host nervously guessing about who is invited.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have been invited to a party or event are its visitors, the synonym here.

clue.text: Appends public notices, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is heard aloud, so a soundalike for the notices word

parts.note: ads are advertisements, public notices

explanation.surface: Someone tacking on public notices, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach at the end, the same as to put on more.

clue.text: Curiously sift ideas for content

indicators.note: curiously signals that the letters of sift ideas are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Advice to sort through ideas in search of something to fill an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like a noun (subject matter) but is the adjective meaning pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Being content means happy and having what one wants, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Motif in anthem emerged

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: A musical motif came through in the anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring idea or subject in a work of art is a motif; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Questions fool about king

indicators.note: about says the word for fool wraps around the letter for king

parts.note: an ass is a fool
K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A court jester questioning the monarch about his rule.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, questions means inquires of someone, the same as the answer in the third person.

clue.text: Give up on French and translate

parts.note: sur is French for on
to render a text into another language is to translate it

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit working on a French translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding or capitulating is giving up; the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Achievement of one who inherits disregarding gold

indicators.note: disregarding says the gold is ignored, i.e. dropped from the heir's word

parts.note: a successor is one who inherits a title or estate
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An heir whose real achievement has nothing to do with money.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, the heraldic word for gold, is the convention the solver needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplishment or triumph is an achievement, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drunk is seen outside British Library, initially sober

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters go around the initials
drunk signals the letters of is seen are reeling into a new order
initially takes the first letters of British and Library

explanation.surface: A drunk spotted outside the British Library, sobering up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' and 'sober' sit as opposites in the surface; 'Drunk' is the anagram indicator, making SENSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober, as in a level-headed choice, means practical and reasonable.

clue.text: Lacking knowledge, I storm angrily about disorderly NGO

indicators.note: disorderly says the letters of NGO are mixed up

parts.note: to rant about something is to storm angrily about it

explanation.surface: An activist furiously railing against a chaotic charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without education or information is uninformed, unknowing: the phrase is a paraphrase.

clue.text: Enthusiastically performing gay reel

indicators.note: performing signals the letters of gay reel are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Dancers keenly performing a merry Scottish reel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gay' here is the old sense, merry; a reel is a lively Scottish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something keenly and with relish is doing it enthusiastically: adverb synonyms.

clue.text: Tale that might be spun?

definitions.meaning: a story, especially a long rambling one
thread twisted from fibres on a wheel; also hints at spinning a story

explanation.definitionFit: A long tall story is called a yarn, and wool for knitting is spun into thread.

clue.text: Reportedly apprehend witnesses

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than read, so we want a word sounding like the one for apprehend

parts.note: to apprehend a criminal is to seize them

explanation.surface: Police said to arrest the witnesses of a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, witnesses means observes or notices, a synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Shock cleaner?

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it, and this liquid washes hair

explanation.definitionFit: A product for washing hair cleans a shock, i.e. a thick head of hair.

clue.text: Refined central European possessing personal magnetism

indicators.note: possessing says the European holds the charisma word inside

parts.note: a Pole is from Poland in central Europe
it is slang for sex appeal or charisma

explanation.surface: A cultured Polish person with charisma.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-mannered and courteous, refined and polite are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Appearance of messy patches husband abandoned

indicators.note: messy says the remaining letters are jumbled
abandoned says the husband letter is left out of patches

explanation.surface: A wife whose clothes look messily patched after her husband left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops H from PATCHES; 'messy' rearranges PATCES.
explanation.definitionFit: The look or face something presents is its appearance, a synonym.

clue.text: Cure small donkey

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A remedy for a little donkey's ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' looks like a medical noun but is the verb for preserving fish or meat by fumes. MOKE is old British slang for donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure fish or bacon over burning wood is to preserve it with fumes; the verbs match.

clue.text: Advancing copyright in designs produces these responses

indicators.note: advancing says the copyright letter moves further along within the word for designs

parts.note: designs are creations
C is the abbreviation for copyright, from the symbol

explanation.surface: Moving forward with copyright protection on designs provokes responses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advancing' moves the C of CREATIONS three places later.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies or answers to a stimulus are responses; the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Unsure about husband's old character

indicators.note: about says the word for unsure wraps around the letter for husband

parts.note: torn means unable to decide, unsure

explanation.surface: Doubts about a husband's past personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter, not personality: an Old English and Icelandic letter for 'th'.
explanation.definitionFit: A runic letter used in Old English is an obsolete alphabet symbol.

clue.text: Labels balance sheet including Durban's currency

indicators.note: including says the abbreviation for balance sheet holds the currency inside it

parts.note: BS is the accounting abbreviation for balance sheet
Durban is in South Africa, whose currency is the rand

explanation.surface: Accountants labelling a balance sheet that lists amounts in South African money.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade names or marks on goods are brands, synonyms for the noun labels.

clue.text: Contrary to work attitude about technology

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: about says the word for attitude goes around the letters for technology

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or stance
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: An employee whose stance on technology at work is contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary and opposite both mean directly against or reverse; adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Absolute anger pursuing field of medicine

indicators.note: pursuing says the word for anger chases, so comes after, the medical field

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a medical specialty
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Pure fury chasing a branch of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete, whole, total: absolute and entire share the sense of without limit.

clue.text: Most recently arrived surprisingly gutsy one

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of gutsy one turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A newcomer who turns out to be surprisingly brave.
explanation.definitionFit: The baby of a family is the latest born, the one who arrived last: a descriptive paraphrase.
